requirements.text: Identify one entity responsible for contract performance. Joint or combined proposals from two or more offerors are not responsive.
Use the Supplier Portal with a registered Bidder ID and finish submission by the stated deadline; other submission methods and late uploads are not accepted.
Address every item; submit the executive-summary letter, each response item and attachments as separate standalone files, preserving the original attachment formats.
Return both the Artificial Intelligence Technical Proposal Questions and Infrastructure Overview, together with the executive summary and Attachments D, E, F and J.
Provide evidence that the executive-summary signer can bind the respondent, such as bylaws or a board resolution, and the required organizational identifiers and response contact information.
Describe the respondent's legal form, formation state, certificate of authority, business activities and organization chart, including the responsible product division where applicable.

Provide financial-stability documents: a recent D&B report is preferred, or two completed fiscal years of audited statements. If neither is available, explain why and provide income statements and balance sheets for those years. Parent-company evidence needs respondent-specific relationship and stability information.

Include a statement that the responding entity's CEO and/or CFO takes responsibility for the completeness and correctness of the supplied financial information, with the requested governance information.
Attachment E section 14, Evidence of Financial Responsibility, is expressly removed at the agency's request. This does not remove the separate financial-stability information requested by section 3.
Describe government-service experience and provide named examples of clients with comparable size and scope; the Business and Technical Proposals form the management/quality evaluation.

Provide three Attachment H references from clients for whom the respondent provided the same or similar services. Clients complete and send their forms directly to the State; receipt is due October 28, 2026 at 3:00 PM Eastern Time.

If subcontractors are proposed, disclose every subcontractor, workshare, qualifications, contractual relationship and anticipated amount. Include an executed subcontract or signed letter of agreement; combined qualifications may be evaluated, while the respondent remains responsible.
Attachment I is an optional networking form. The State encourages it, but the RFP does not require its submission.

The IVOSB goal is 3% and affects evaluation points. If participation is proposed, provide Attachment A and valid certification by the proposal due date; its bid total must match Attachment D. Zero participation deducts one point rather than creating a stated universal participation condition.
Buy Indiana points require an affirmative claim and finalized status at sourcing-event submission. The form permits a respondent to decline the claim.

Review the sample contract and any applicable IaaS, PaaS and SaaS terms. Submit any permitted proposed changes with the proposal as tracked redlines and explanations; later changes are not assured and the State may reject proposed language.

If awarded, the covered organization types must register and be in good standing with Indiana's Secretary of State. Report current status in Attachment J; the RFP places the registration obligation at award.
The respondent must not have had a State contract or purchase order terminated or cancelled in the last two calendar years for failure to deliver in accordance with its terms.

Review the State-action, payment-arrears and conflict-of-interest representations before any response. Participation in preparing the solicitation, including the specified recent-hire circumstance, bars responding under the stated provision.

For proposed IT products or services, establish compatibility with applicable State IT policies and the assistive-technology standard, and address the RFP's ADA compliance requirement. Sensitive standards may require a contractor NDA.
The base contract term is two years from execution, with two optional one-year extensions at the State's discretion.

Propose MAC framework modernization, redesigned and piloted time-study tools with FSSA and AAAs, standardized cost-reporting and cost-pooling processes, and support for AAA monitoring and quality improvement.

Provide a plan for MAC claiming operations and error-free claim files during the base term and any extensions, stakeholder support, additional-agency onboarding when directed, and preparation for State operation.

Provide a State-reviewable project plan with deadlines, staffing, communications and risks. Required outputs include activity catalog, time-study tool, training, cost-reporting guidance, operational reports, evaluation summaries, recommendations and transition materials.

Plan for the stated minimum of 95% on-time submissions against the approved project plan and the quality, federal compliance, operational reliability, stakeholder-support and stewardship KPIs. Other details are finalized collaboratively; underperformance may lead to a corrective-action plan or payment delay.
Payments depend on deliverable acceptance. If the State employs IV&V, its approval precedes payment, and the contractor provides the IV&V team the required communications and access.

At the end of the base term or an extension, transfer the tools, artifacts and documentation, conduct knowledge transfer, support uninterrupted State operations, and deliver recommendations and a final transition/readiness report.

Answer separately for AI in the proposed solution and AI used by developers during implementation/support: use, disablement and consequences, control of functionality, and four-year introduction/expansion plans. The form also provides no-current-use/no-planned-use response paths.

State whether hosting is in scope. For hosting proposals, the State prefers a State-owned cloud tenant; justified alternatives may be considered. Cloud offerings must satisfy IOT Policy P.05 at implementation, and the form permits N/A for an unproposed hosting category.

If proposing a State-owned cloud tenant, address State ownership/control, residency of all solution data in that tenant, approved native monitoring/backup/recovery tools, access controls and encryption, audit/security reporting, and transition back to the State.

If proposing a vendor-owned cloud exception, justify why a State-owned tenant is infeasible and provide independently verified NIST 800-53 Revision 5 compliance, or a detailed path with independent verification, using the version current at go-live and the applicable cloud terms.

Report whether the company has a business-continuity/disaster-recovery plan and attach it if present; otherwise explain its alternative. Describe how State information maintained by the company is secured.

Use Attachment D in its original format, with a PDF cost narrative of no more than two pages for each item and a separate assumptions/conditions/constraints PDF. Costs must correspond to the technical response; conflicting assumptions or caveats are not acceptable.
Proposed pricing must be firm and remain open for at least 180 days from award issuance.

If claiming confidential treatment, identify the specific APRA exception, affected document/section and rationale in Attachment J and provide the applicable separate redacted/confidential version. A blanket section label is insufficient.
Written questions are due October 7, 2026 at 3:00 PM Eastern Time; responses/amendments are scheduled for October 14. Only posted written answers and addenda are binding.
Evaluation first checks mandatory requirements, then management/quality (50 points) and cost (30), with Buy Indiana (5), IVOSB (5) and a possible additional IVOSB point as specified.
